title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 202 (Compensation for loss of office of managing or whole-time director or manager)

content.overview: Section 202 allows a company to make payment to a managing director, whole-time director or manager by way of compensation for loss of office, or as consideration for retirement from office, or in connection with such loss or retirement. No such payment shall be made in the cases prohibited by the section (including resignation, removal for specified defaults, winding-up on certain grounds, and reconstruction/amalgamation where the person is reappointed). The amount must not exceed the remuneration that would have been earned for the unexpired residue of the term or for three years, whichever is shorter, calculated on the average remuneration actually earned during a specified preceding period. Payment requires approval as the section provides.
content.glance: MD/WTD/manager may receive loss-of-office compensation except in prohibited cases (resignation, certain defaults, certain windings-up, reappointment on reconstruction); cap = shorter of unexpired term or 3 years of average remuneration; approval as section requires.
content.study: A company may make payment to a managing or whole-time director or manager, by way of compensation for loss of office, or as consideration for retirement from office, or in connection with such loss or retirement. No payment shall be made in the cases listed (including where the director resigns from office; where the office is lost by virtue of reconstruction or amalgamation and the person is reappointed; where the office is lost by virtue of winding-up on grounds of insolvency or certain other specified grounds; where the director has been guilty of fraud or breach of trust or specified defaults). The amount shall not exceed the remuneration which he would have earned if he had been in office for the unexpired residue of his term or for three years, whichever is shorter, calculated on the basis of the average remuneration actually earned by him during a period of three years immediately preceding the date on which he ceased to hold office, or where he held office for a lesser period, during such period. Current-law framing: identify MD/WTD/manager and proposed loss-of-office payment; exclude prohibited cases; apply the average-remuneration cap (shorter of unexpired term or three years); secure the approval the section requires. Distinguish transfer-linked payments under s. 191.

sections.heading: Permitted Payment
sections.body: Company may pay MD, WTD or manager compensation for loss of office, or consideration for retirement, or in connection with such loss or retirement.

sections.heading: Prohibited Cases
sections.body: No payment where the person resigns; loses office on reconstruction/amalgamation with reappointment; loses office on specified winding-up grounds; or is guilty of fraud, breach of trust or specified defaults.

sections.heading: Cap
sections.body: Not exceeding remuneration for the unexpired residue of the term or for three years, whichever is shorter, based on average remuneration actually earned in the preceding three years (or lesser period held).

sections.heading: Approval
sections.body: Payment requires the approval the section states; does not override other limits such as s. 197.

provisions.title: Compensation for loss of office of managing or whole-time director or manager

examples.title: Resignation — no compensation
examples.body: An MD resigns mid-term and claims loss-of-office compensation. Section 202 prohibits payment where the director resigns from office.

examples.title: Cap calculation
examples.body: A WTD with two years of unexpired term and average annual remuneration of ₹50 lakh over the preceding three years may, if otherwise eligible, receive up to the shorter of two years’ or three years’ average — i.e. up to ₹1 crore — not an open-ended golden handshake.

hypotheticals.question: May a company pay unlimited loss-of-office compensation to an MD removed without default?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Even when payment is not prohibited, the amount is capped at the shorter of the unexpired term or three years of average remuneration actually earned. Other limits (including s. 197) may also apply.

distinctions.title: Loss-of-office compensation (s. 202) vs transfer-linked payment (s. 191)
distinctions.left: General compensation for loss of office of MD/WTD/manager with statutory cap and prohibited cases
distinctions.right: Payments linked to transfer of undertaking/property/shares; disclosure and GM approval

misconceptions.trap: Any departing MD is entitled to loss-of-office compensation as of right.
misconceptions.correction: Section 202 permits payment only outside the prohibited cases and only within the average-remuneration cap; resignation and certain defaults bar payment.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 202 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm MD/WTD/manager and proposed payment. II. Exclude prohibited cases. III. Apply average-remuneration cap. IV. Check approval. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Office facts; prohibition test; cap calculation; approval; precise relief.

examTips: Prohibited cases first (resignation, defaults, certain windings-up).
Cap = shorter of unexpired term or 3 years’ average pay.
content.migrationNote: Substantive enhancement. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

learningObjectives: State when loss-of-office compensation may be paid under s. 202.
Apply the prohibited cases and the average-remuneration cap.
enhancement.definition: Section 202 permits limited compensation for loss of office of an MD, WTD or manager, subject to prohibited cases and a cap based on average remuneration for the shorter of the unexpired term or three years.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Golden handshakes for managerial personnel are tightly capped and barred where the office is lost by resignation or default.
essentialIngredients: Payment to MD/WTD/manager for loss of office or retirement
Cap: shorter of unexpired term or 3 years’ average remuneration
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 202 is the general loss-of-office compensation rule for managerial personnel, distinct from transfer-linked payments under s. 191.
enhancement.problemApplication: Test prohibition; compute cap; check approval.

verification.note: Section-text level; full list of prohibited cases is in the Act; case-law verification separate; no new citations invented.
